I've always been fascinated by the night sky. As a child, I'd spend hours lying on my back in the grass, staring up at the stars, trying to connect the dots to form constellations. My favorite was Orion, the hunter, with his distinctive belt and sword. I'd imagine him striding across the cosmos, chasing comets and nebulae.

Now, as an adult, I still find myself drawn to the night sky. But now, I understand the science behind it. I know that those twinkling points of light are suns, some much larger and brighter than our own, others tiny and dim. I know that the Milky Way, that hazy band of light that stretches across the sky, is our galaxy, a spiral of stars and planets and dust, hurtling through space at a million miles an hour.

I think about the vastness of it all, the scale that defies comprehension. I think about the trillions of stars out there, each one a sun to countless planets, each one a world that might harbor life. I think about the light-years between us, the distances so great that even at the speed of light, it would take thousands of years to cross.

And yet, despite the immensity of it all, I feel small but not insignificant. I'm just one person, one tiny speck of life on one tiny planet, orbiting one tiny star. But I'm part of something bigger, something beautiful and awe-inspiring. I'm part of the universe, and that's enough to make me feel connected, to make me feel at home.
